common_name: Loyalist Hosta (White-Centered Dark Green-Margined Reverse Patriot Sport)

planting.note: Divide and transplant dormant crowns in early spring or early fall, setting the crown at the same depth it grew previously in moist, humus-rich soil. Loyalist is a reverse-variegated sport of the popular Patriot, with a white center and dark green margin.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in a partly to fully shaded site, setting the crown at the same depth it grew previously and watering well until established. Loyalist arose as a reverse-variegated sport of the popular Patriot hosta, flipping the pattern so a bright white center is surrounded by a dark green margin, a striking inversion of its well-known parent's coloring. It produces lavender flowers on tall scapes in summer, though the bold, high-contrast foliage is the primary ornamental feature. Mulch to conserve moisture and protect the shallow root system from summer heat, and divide congested clumps every several years in spring.

It produces lavender flowers on tall scapes in summer. Mulch to conserve moisture and protect the shallow root system from summer heat, and divide congested clumps every several years in spring.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in a partly to fully shaded site, setting the crown at the same depth it grew previously and watering well until established. Dancing Queen, a striking sport of the widely grown Paul's Glory, bears solid gold leaves with intensely rippled, glossy, undulating surfaces that catch the light beautifully, a bold, glowing color and texture combination for a shaded border. common_name: Cherry Berry Hosta (Miniature White-Centered Hosta with Red Petioles)

planting.note: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Cherry Berry is a miniature hosta with white-centered green leaves and bright red petioles and flower scapes, an unusual color trait for the genus.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Cherry Berry is a diminutive miniature hosta bearing small, white-centered green leaves, but its standout trait is the bright cherry-red coloring of its petioles and flower scapes, an unusual and eye-catching feature rare among hosta cultivars. Its tiny mature size fits containers, rock gardens, and the front edge of a shaded border. Divide clumps every four to five years in spring if increased numbers are wanted, since the compact habit means division is rarely necessary for plant health.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Pandora's Box is a diminutive miniature hosta bearing small leaves with bright white centers edged in a narrow green margin, a high-contrast variegation pattern packed into a tiny mature footprint.
